finding_key: packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts::no way to re-base `undofloor`; a yorkie snapshot that resets the undo stack can leave notes permanently un-undoable
evidence: The factual part of the claim checks out: `undoFloor` is set once in the constructor (`yorkie-note-store.ts`, `this.undoFloor = doc.getUndoStackForTest().length`) and never re-based, and `notes-view.tsx` builds the store only on `[didMount, doc]`, so nothing recaptures it. But the defect itself rests on an unverified premise — that applying a Yorkie snapshot clears the client's undo stack. As far as I can tell from the SDK's design (`applySnapshot` replaces root/clone and publishes a `snapshot` event; clearing history is a separate explicit `doc.clearHistory()` API, which notes calls only in `ensureText()` *before* the store is constructed), snapshot application does not reset `history`, so the stack length cannot drop below the recorded floor; the reviewer also states outright they could not confirm this. Even granting the premise, the described impact is overstated: after a reset to 0, new local edits push entries back and `canUndo()` (`length > undoFloor`, floor typically 1 from the attach seed) becomes true again, so at most the earliest floor-many edits become non-undoable rather than undo being "silently disabled for the session". I could not read `@yorkie-js/sdk` in this environment, hence low confidence.
